strawberry.originalMethod: Unmodified protected smoke test, headless SwiftShader, Chromium, one page at a time. Both comparison sources time out at the 15-second return-to-rest predicate. Final-candidate Mesa results are in required, not this earlier comparison.
strawberry.probeMethod: DISPLAY=:94 LP_NUM_THREADS=2 SPLASHERY_GL=llvmpipe. Wraps player.update only to record dt; leaves production time, controls, camera, and geometry unchanged. Rest/pop/settled screenshots compare RGB differences above 24, as the original smoke predicate does. Each source uses its normal scene seed; these are within-source return-to-rest comparisons, not cross-source pixel identity proof.
strawberry.cause: The unchanged native update caps dt at 0.1 seconds; pulse decay advances in simulation time, while the smoke predicate has a 15-second wall-time budget. Both sources eventually return to rest in the probe. However, the later controlled Mesa comparison passes on main and on the raw candidate, while the compressed candidate fails. No exact engine-byte, module-export, rig, or relative-worker difference was found. The homepage retains its original HTTP engine module, but a later original-test rerun still fails. An external fixture observer then records both latest main and candidate failing before the pulse completes. The homepage fallback is not a demonstrated fix; the subsequent native-entry commit restores the original HTTP engine globally. This observation diagnoses unfinished simulation time and does not establish a production animation defect or a demonstrated timing fix.
